questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, what is the best way to make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well (at dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights. This makes your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: Tires that are different sizes:

options.text: Can be used only on a front axle.
Can be used only on a trailer's axles.

questions.explanation: All tires on your vehicle must be the same size. Check that your tires match when you inspect your vehicle.

questions.question: You should sign a previous driver's vehicle inspection report if:

options.text: The previous driver dated their entry.
Any reported defects have been fixed.
You plan to drive for longer than one hour or travel farther than 50 miles.
The report is left on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any reported defects have been fixed.
questions.explanation: Sign a previous inspection report only if defects were fixed or if no repairs were needed.

questions.question: The most steering wheel movement that is safe on a 20-inch wheel is:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of movement may not be safe. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of play at the rim.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, drivers must check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the smallest size allowed for a hazard placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous material placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Choose your own route to show your driving skills.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.explanation: Follow the directions given by the examiner during the on-road driving test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: After a trip, you should:

options.text: Place the vehicle out of service.

questions.explanation: After a trip, you may need to inspect the vehicle and file a report.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should speed up slowly:

options.text: Because it is always best to accelerate very slowly.
So they keep control of their vehicle.
So they do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they keep control of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too fast on a slippery road can cause you to lose control. Always accelerate slowly and smoothly when traction is poor.

questions.question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down by itself. Once it slows down enough, brake gently, move off the road, and stop.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The vehicle is easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when the tires lift off the road and slide on a layer of water instead.

questions.question: Before driving a bus, you must:

options.text: Check the most recent inspection report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the most recent inspection report.
questions.explanation: Always inspect a bus before driving it. You must read the inspection report from the previous driver. Only drive the bus if any problems listed have been fixed or do not need to be fixed.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not recommended. It can damage the vehicle.
Not recommended. It may confuse other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended. It can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and slowly. Rough acceleration can harm the vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: If driving in fog, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers. Never speed up in fog.

questions.question: To put out an electrical fire, use:

options.text: A B or C fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: A B or C fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: Use B or C type fire extinguishers on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: Good drivers look ahead ____ seconds before their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to react to dangers before you reach them.

questions.question: The emergency exit door:

options.text: Can be opened if the bus gets too hot while being driven.
Can be opened while the bus is moving if it carries cargo.
Can be opened while backing the bus to see better.
Should never be open while the bus is being driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be open while the bus is being driven.
questions.explanation: Check all emergency exits before you drive. Never drive a bus with an open emergency exit door or window.

questions.question: If stopped on the road or shoulder, you must place emergency warning devices within:

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and signal traffic to pass.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, place warning triangles or other warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.
